entries.title: Player AI Assistant: your own companion
q: what is the player ai assistant
a helper that plays like a player
entries.answer: Your Player AI Assistant is a companion of your own: it talks with you, takes orders in plain words or by voice, and plays like a player.
more: It chops, mines, farms, crafts the whole chain, smelts, builds the mod's buildings, fights, fetches and tidies, and grows better with use.
It belongs to you alone: it is not one of the village folk, takes no town job and draws no wage.
It never fights people: a knock from you does it no harm, and it only ever fights monsters.
steps: Press Y (or right-click your assistant) to open its panel.
Type what you want in the Talk tab, click an order, or hold Z and say it.
tips: Ask it "what can you do?" for a list, or "what are you doing?" any time.

entries.title: Getting your Player AI Assistant
q: how do i get an ai assistant
how do i get my assistant
how do i get a player ai assistant
how do i make an assistant
entries.answer: Press Y and click Get my assistant: the first one is free. Or craft an Assistant Whistle, or place an Assistant Spawner and click it.
more: Assistant Whistle: 4 iron ingots in the corners, 4 redstone on the sides, a gold ingot in the middle. Use it on the ground and your assistant appears there; blown later, it calls your assistant to you at once.

Assistant Spawner: 8 rotten flesh round a diamond. Place it and click it: your assistant comes out, and the spawner is its home and the place it comes back to if it falls. A sneak-click on the spawner hires a crew hand instead.
However it appears, it is yours for good: it shows your name, obeys only you (and operators), and follows you through logouts and into other dimensions.
Each player may have one (the server's operator can allow more). At the limit you are told to dismiss the one you have first.
steps: Press Y: with no assistant yet, the panel offers one.
Click Get my assistant.
It says hello and offers a short tour.
tips: The U page has a Player AI Assistant button too.

entries.title: Talking to your assistant
q: how do i talk to my assistant
how do i give my assistant orders
what can i say to my assistant
tell the assistant what to do
entries.answer: Open its panel (Y) and type in the Talk tab as you would to a person; it answers in words, aloud, and in a bubble over its head.
more: It reads typos and slang, and chains steps: "chop 64 logs, then make planks and sticks, then build a crafting table by my house".
"Here", "there" and "that" mean what you are looking at: look at a chest and say "put everything in that chest".
Before a long or big job it checks with you (OK, Change, Cancel). "Stop" and "undo" always work at once.
Ask it about the mod too ("how do I start a business?"): it answers from the Guide.
When it isn't sure what you mean, it asks back with choices to click: it never just ignores you.
steps: Press Y.
Type an order such as "get me 16 logs" and press Enter, or click one of the suggestions under the box.
tips: The suggestions change with what you look at and hold, and the time of day.
No chat is used: everything is in its own panel.

entries.title: The assistant's Orders tab
q: make my assistant build a house
how do i make my assistant follow me
entries.answer: The Orders tab has a button for each common job; the ones with choices ask how many and where, then send the order.
more: Follow, Stay, Come, Guard me, Guard here, Gather wood or stone, Mine ore, Mine down, Farm, Build, Craft, Smelt, Deposit, Fight, Bring food, Light up, Sort chests, Go home, Stop.
It gets what a job needs first, as a player would: a pickaxe before stone, the blocks and the furniture before a house, a hoe and seeds before a field.
steps: Press Y and open Orders.
Click an order; pick the amount and the place if it asks.
Click Go: its answer shows in Talk.
tips: Building uses the same drawings and builder as the towns, so its houses look as good.

entries.title: The assistant's action wheel (X)
q: tell the assistant to mine this
entries.answer: Look at something and press X: the wheel offers what fits it first (mine this vein, use that chest, attack that, farm this field, build there).
more: Click a choice, or hold X, point and let go. The everyday orders (come, follow, guard, stay, stop) are round the rest of it.
steps: Look at a block, a chest or a creature.
Press X and pick what your assistant should do with it.

entries.title: What your assistant is doing (Jobs)
entries.answer: The Jobs tab lists what it is doing now and next, with progress and a time; move any up or down, cancel it, or pause them all.
more: A small line at the top left of the screen shows what it is doing too ("Chopping logs 12/16"); switch it off in About.
When it can't do something it says why and offers a fix to click ("I need a pickaxe: make one?").
Small snags it sorts out itself, as a player would: it makes a new pickaxe when one wears out, climbs out of a pit it dug, and walks to the nearest trees it can see when none are close.
steps: Press Y and open Jobs.
Use the arrows to reorder, the cross to cancel, Pause to hold the list.
tips: Say "stop" to stop everything at once, or "undo" to take back your last order.

entries.title: Talking to your assistant by voice
q: how do i talk to my assistant with my voice
entries.answer: Turn on Listen in your assistant's About tab, then hold Z and speak: your words go to it like a typed order.
more: On Windows it uses Windows' own offline speech recognition. Elsewhere (or if that's missing) it asks to download a small offline speech model (about 40 MB, once) into your config folder.
It speaks its replies with your computer's own voice: pick the voice, speed and volume in About, or switch speaking off. Its words always show as well.
Only the recognised words go to the server: no sound leaves your computer.

Accent: English (UK), English (US) or Auto in About. On Windows it uses the UK recogniser when installed. The offline model is US English (there is no small British one), so it listens for its own phrases, which copes well with a British accent.
steps: Press Y, open About and switch Listen on (agree to the download if it asks).
Close the panel, hold Z, say "follow me", let go.
tips: A light and your words as they are heard show above the hotbar while you hold the key.

entries.title: Auto-help: your assistant on its own
q: what does my assistant do on its own
stop my assistant doing things on its own
entries.answer: With nothing to do and auto-help on, it does useful things for you and says what and why; click Don't do that to veto one.
more: It steps in when something hostile comes at you, puts a full pack away, keeps a cold furnace fuelled, picks ripe crops, brings you food if you have none, lights dark ground at night, and now and then sorts the chests at home.
Switch it off in About, or say "only do what I say".
steps: Press Y, open About, and set Auto-help on or off.
tips: Anything you ask comes first: it drops what it chose to do.

entries.title: Your assistant's settings (About)
entries.answer: The About tab shows its level and record and holds every setting: name, look, personality, voice, chattiness, auto-help, chests and roaming.
more: Chattiness: Quiet, Low, Normal or Chatty (it always answers you). Ask before big jobs, may use your chests, may break blocks near your builds, shelter at night, how far it roams, and how much it may spend at a market for you.
Personalities: Cheerful, Dry or Calm. Looks: eight outfits.
steps: Press Y and open About.
Click a setting to change it.
tips: Replay the tour from About any time.

entries.title: If your assistant falls, or is far away
q: assistant didnt follow me to the nether
entries.answer: A fallen assistant comes back after a minute, at its spawner or beside you, keeping its pack. A whistle brings it back at once.
more: It leaves with you when you log out and is beside you when you're back; it follows you through portals unless it is busy or told to stay.
Far away or lost in an unloaded place? The summon button in its panel, or a blown whistle, calls it to you.
steps: Press Y: the panel says when it will be back.
Or use an Assistant Whistle: no waiting.
tips: It gets itself out of trouble too: stuck, in lava or drowning, it comes back to you.

entries.title: Your assistant is yours, not a villager
q: does my assistant count as folk
will the town hire my assistant
difference between my assistant and the folk
can my assistant join a town
entries.answer: Your assistant is entirely separate from the village folk: it is never a citizen, takes no town job, home or wage, and works only for you.
more: Towns don't count it among their folk or hire it, and their guards treat it as your companion.
It respects other people's ground: it won't break, build or open chests on a town's ground or in someone else's land unless the server allows it.

entries.title: Troubleshooting your assistant's voice
entries.answer: Check Listen is on in About and the talk key is Z; the footer and the line above the hotbar say what's wrong. Typing always works.
more: "No microphone found": the game can't reach your microphone; check your system's privacy settings let Java use it.
No speech heard on Linux or macOS: turn Listen on and agree to the model download (it needs the internet once).
Silent replies: on Linux install espeak-ng; on Windows and macOS the system's own voice is used. Speaking can be switched on in About.
steps: Press Y, open About, look at the line under Listen and under Speak.

entries.title: Your assistant's personality (the triangle)
entries.answer: In About, drag the dot in the triangle: Serious at the top, Funny bottom left, Gloomy bottom right. Anywhere between mixes them.
more: Presets snap it: Professional, Banter, Joker, Doom and Balanced. A sample line shows what it'll sound like.
Chattiness sets how often it speaks unasked. At "Won't shut up" with the dot at Funny it becomes the Joke Machine: a remark on what you're doing every 10 to 20 seconds.
Warnings are always said plainly first. When you die it says where your things are and offers to fetch them.
Say "tell me a joke", or give it some lip; it answers in kind and still does the job.
steps: Press Y and open the About tab.
Drag the dot, or click a preset; set Chattiness underneath.
tips: Gloomy is comic pessimism about chores and weather; it still does every job properly.

entries.title: Choosing your assistant's look
entries.answer: Open the Look tab and click a look: 18 to choose from, including a skeleton, a zombie, a creeper hoodie and a tall enderman.
more: Changing is free and instant, and everyone sees it. Drag the preview to turn it round.
Each look brings a few remarks of its own, and some about itself, about one remark in five.
steps: Press Y and open the Look tab.
Click a look in the list.
tips: The skeleton is very aware it's built like a chopstick.

entries.title: Natural-sounding voices for your assistant
entries.answer: Its voice is yours to choose: every voice on your computer is listed, the most natural first, each with a preview.
more: Windows: it prefers the modern voices (Hazel, George and Susan for UK English). Add more in Settings > Time & language > Speech. Windows 11's Narrator natural voices are only for Narrator and can't be used by other apps.
Mac: download an Enhanced or Premium voice in System Settings > Accessibility > Spoken Content > System voice > Manage Voices.
Linux uses espeak: it works, but sounds basic.

The most human voices: click Get natural British voices under Voice. These are Kokoro voices (George, Lewis, Daniel, Fable, Emma, Isabella, Alice, Lily) that run offline. They are only downloaded if you agree: about 213 MB, once, from GitHub and Maven Central (Kokoro is Apache-2.0, ONNX Runtime is MIT). They also need the free program eSpeak NG on your computer.
With them, each look gets a fitting voice: George for the knight, Fable for the butler, Daniel for the skeleton. Pick a woman's voice (Emma or Isabella) and the suggestions follow.
Speed and pitch are in About too, and a gloomy assistant speaks slower and lower.
steps: Press Y, open About, click Voice.
Press the play button beside a voice to hear it.
tips: Leave it on Auto and it picks the most natural voice for your accent.

entries.title: Voice with a British (or other) accent
q: my assistant doesnt understand my accent
entries.answer: Set Accent to English (UK) in About. On Windows, add the UK English speech pack; then use short orders and keep your mic level steady.
more: Windows: Settings > Time & language > Speech, and add English (United Kingdom). The About tab says which recogniser is in use.
Train Windows to your voice: Control Panel > Speech Recognition > Train your computer to better understand you.
Short orders work best ("follow me", "get us 16 logs", "bung it in the chest"): they match its phrase list, which copes with any accent.
Speak at your usual pace with the mic close; the level light above the hotbar should move but not stay full.
With UK set it also speaks in a British voice if your computer has one (Hazel or George on Windows, Daniel or Kate on a Mac).
steps: Press Y and open the About tab; click Accent until it reads English (UK).
Read the line under Listen: it names the recogniser and how to add the UK one.
tips: Mis-hears like "lugs" for logs or "fallow" for follow are put right for spoken orders.
